title: AntRep — The Complete Guide
subtitle: Everything the app does, in plain language. Start at the top, or jump to the part you need.
edition: Covers the athlete portal and the coach portal.

parts.title: 1. Start here
parts.intro: AntRep is a training app with two sides. Athletes follow a plan and log what they lift. Coaches build those plans and read the numbers that come back. Both sides live in the same app, and one account can be both.

sections.title: The two sides
body: The athlete portal is the main app. It opens at the web address on its own — nothing extra after the slash.
The coach portal is the same app with /coach on the end of the address. It has its own sign-in and its own tabs.

head: Side
Where
What it's for
rows: Following a plan, logging sets, watching your numbers
Building plans, inviting athletes, reading their training

sections.title: Try it first, no account needed
body: On the sign-in screen there's a button that says "Explore the demo without an account". Tap it and you get a fully stocked practice account with months of fake training already in it.
The demo lives only in your browser. Nothing is sent anywhere, and nothing you do there touches a real account. It's the best way to click around before you commit.
sections.tip: The demo also has a ready-made coach account, so you can see both sides.

sections.title: Making your account
steps: Open the portal you want — plain address for athlete, /coach for coach.
Tap "Create account".
Type your name, your email, and a password of at least 8 characters.
Tap the create button.
body: You sign up for one side at a time. Signing up on the athlete side gives you an athlete profile; the coach side gives you a coach profile.

sections.title: "Waiting for approval"
body: On a real (non-demo) setup, a brand new profile has to be switched on by whoever runs the app before you can use it. If you see a screen that says your profile has been created and is waiting, that's all this is.
Nothing is wrong and nothing is lost. Ask whoever set up AntRep for you to approve it, then sign in again.

sections.title: Being an athlete and a coach at once
body: You don't need two accounts. Go to Settings, scroll to the Account section, and tap the row at the top.

If you only have one side so far it will say "Become a coach too" (or "Become an athlete too") and set the other side up for you. After that the same row switches you between the two whenever you want.
Coaches who train themselves use the "My training" tab instead — see part 5.

parts.title: 2. Athlete — your first week
parts.intro: If you read only one part, read this one. It takes you from an empty account to a logged workout.

sections.title: Step 1 — get a plan
body: A plan is your training week: which days you train, and what you do on each. You can get one two ways.

From a coach: ask them for an invite code, then go to Settings and find the Coaches box. Type the code and tap Link. Their plans then appear on the Plans tab, where you tap Sync to start following one.
On your own: go to the Plans tab and tap New. Give the plan a name and a start date, then fill in the days you want to train.
sections.tip: No coach and no plan is fine too — you can log loose workouts from day one using "Extra work" on the Home screen.

sections.title: Step 2 — open today
body: The Home tab always opens on today. Under the greeting you'll see a card for each block of work scheduled for today — for example a "Push day" card and a "Walk, run or jog" card.
Each card shows how far through it you are, like 0/5 exercises.

sections.title: Step 3 — start the workout
body: Tap "Start now" on the day card. You get three choices.

head: Choice
What happens
rows: A timer runs while you train. Best for a normal session.
Pick a different day of your plan to do today.
No clock. Best when you're writing up a session afterwards.

sections.title: Step 4 — log your sets
steps: Tap an exercise to open it.
Tap "Add set" for each set you do.
Fill in the boxes. Use the − and + buttons, or tap the number and type it.
When the exercise is done, tap the tick on its right-hand side.
body2: The boxes change to suit the exercise. A barbell lift asks for kilograms and reps; a run asks for kilometres and minutes; a plank asks for seconds.
Decimals are fine. Type 52.5 for a 52.5 kg lift or 3.2 for 3.2 km — just type the dot as part of the number.

sections.title: Step 5 — finish
body: If you used the timer, tap the stop button on the timer bar when you're done. If you didn't, there's nothing to finish — everything is saved the moment you type it.
You earn XP for starting, for each exercise, for each set, and for finishing. That's what fills the level bar at the top of Home.

sections.title: Missed a day?
body: Nothing is lost. Two ways to catch up:
Train it today: on Home, tap "Train another day" and pick the session you missed. It gets logged against today.
Fill it in for the day it happened: use the arrows either side of the date bar on Home to walk back to that day, then log as normal. It saves as a late log, and your streak still counts it.

sections.title: Anything not in the plan
body: Scroll to the bottom of Home and use "Log an exercise" under Extra work. A five-a-side game, a swim, an extra set of curls — it all counts toward your totals and shows up in Progress.
This works on past days too, so you can backfill training you never wrote down.

parts.title: 3. Athlete — every screen
parts.intro: The five tabs along the bottom, plus Settings, in order.

sections.title: Home
body: Today's training, and everything you need to log it.

head: On the screen
What it does
rows: How many days in a row you've trained. Rest days in your plan don't break it.
Your level and XP. Everything you log adds to it.
Exercises done today, sessions this week against your goal, kilograms lifted this week, sessions all time.
Arrows step one day back or forward. Tap the middle to search for a date, or pick from days you've already trained.
One per block of work scheduled that day, with a progress ring.
Appears once a workout is running. Pause, resume, or stop.
Starts after you finish a set, if the exercise has a rest time.

sections.title: Plans
body: Two lists. "From your coach" holds anything a coach has sent you — tap Sync to start following it, or leave it if you'd rather not.
"My plans" holds the ones you built. Tap one to read it week by week, or tap the pencil to edit it.
steps: Tap New to start a plan.
Give it a name, a start date, and how many week blocks it runs for. Week blocks repeat — a 4-week plan starts over at week 1 after week 4.
For each day of the week, set a title and a type (push, pull, legs, run, rest, and so on).
Add exercises to each day: name, sets, reps, weight, rest, and any notes.
Save.
sections.tip: Building a big plan? Copy the rows out of a spreadsheet and use "Paste from Excel" instead of typing them one by one.

sections.title: Coach
body: Everything between you and your coach, in four tabs.

head: Tab
What it's for
rows: A short weekly form: body weight, sleep, energy, appetite, and any aches.
Numbers your coach wants you to keep — waist, resting heart rate, anything they set up.
What your coach wrote after looking at your training. Read-only for you.

body2: If you don't have a coach yet, this tab tells you how to link one.

sections.title: Progress
body: Your numbers, in three tabs. Above the tabs there's a row of chips — leave it on "Overall" to see everything, or pick a plan to narrow every chart and table below to just that plan.

head: Tab
What you get
rows: Weekly goal ring, lifetime totals, a trend chart you can switch between volume, sessions and sets over 4 weeks to 6 months, short read-outs on what changed, muscle balance, and recent records.
Your training as tables. Starts with a card per plan; tap one for its sessions; tap a session for every exercise and every set.
A card per movement you've logged, with a mini trend line, your best, and whether it's going up or down. Search and sort them, then tap one for its full page.

sections.title: Progress — the exercise page
body: Tap any exercise anywhere in Progress and you get its own page: your best, your estimated one-rep max, how many sessions and sets, total volume, a chart you can switch between best, volume and reps, and a full history table.
Tap any row in that history to see the actual sets you did that day.

sections.title: Progress — the session page
body: Tap any session and you get the whole workout: how many exercises, sets, volume and time, your notes, then a table with one row per exercise.

Each row shows your best that day and how it compares to the last time you did that movement. Tap a row to open its individual sets, with RPE if you logged it. Anything the plan asked for that you didn't do is listed too, greyed out.
Use the arrows at the top to step to the session before or after, or tap the middle to jump to a date or pick from the list.

sections.title: Library
body: Every exercise you can log — the built-in catalogue plus anything you've saved. Search it, and tap Save to keep one in your own list.

Saving an exercise also lets you set how it's logged (weight and reps, reps only, distance, time, or your own fields). Whatever you set there is what you'll be asked for every time you log it. That setting lives in Settings under Exercise library.

sections.title: Settings

head: Section
What's in it
rows: Your display name, how many sessions a week you're aiming for, and a weekly distance goal.
Light, dark or automatic, plus an accent colour.
Link a coach with their invite code, and choose whether each one can see your logs.
Set how each saved exercise is logged, and add your own per-set fields.
Switch to the coach side (or create it), and sign out.

sections.tip: The "Share logs with my coach" switch is per coach. Turn it off and they keep the plan connection but stop seeing what you log.

parts.title: 4. Coach — your first week
parts.intro: From an empty coach account to reading an athlete's first session.

sections.title: Step 1 — invite an athlete
steps: Open the Athletes tab.
Tap the button to create an invite code.
Send them the code however you like — message, email, anything.
They enter it in their own Settings, under Coaches.
body: Each code is single-use. Until someone claims it, it sits in a "Waiting to be claimed" list so you can see what's outstanding.

sections.title: Step 2 — build a plan
steps: Open the Plans tab and start a new plan.
Name it, set a start date, and choose how many week blocks it runs.
Fill in the week: give each training day a title and a type, then add exercises.
For each exercise set the sets, reps, target weight, rest, target RPE, and any notes or instructions the athlete should see.
Save.
sections.tip: Already have the programme in a spreadsheet? Use "Paste from Excel" and paste the rows straight in.

sections.title: Step 3 — send it
body: Open the athlete from the Athletes tab, go to the Assign tab, and tap Assign next to the plan.
It doesn't take effect until they sync it from their Plans tab — you'll see the status change from waiting to synced when they do.
You can remove an assignment at any time.

sections.title: Step 4 — read what comes back
body: Open the athlete and use the Overview tab for the quick read: how much of the plan they've done this week, their streak, plan adherence over the last few weeks, lifetime totals, and any records they've set.
Coloured flags at the top call out anything worth a message — missed work, a jump in volume, a movement going backwards.
For the detail, go to the Progress tab. It's the same three tabs the athlete sees, over their data.

sections.title: Step 5 — talk to them
body: The Coaching tab has chat, their check-ins, your notes, and any trackers you've set up. Notes are yours — the athlete can read them but not change them.

parts.title: 5. Coach — every screen
parts.intro: The four tabs along the bottom, and the athlete page behind them.

sections.title: Athletes
body: Your roster. At the top you can make an invite code and see any that haven't been claimed yet. Below that is everyone linked to you, with when they last trained and how many sessions they've done this week.
Tap anyone to open their page.

sections.title: The athlete page

head: Tab
What's in it
rows: This week at a glance, flags worth acting on, plan adherence, lifetime totals, recent records, today's scheduled work, and their latest sessions.
The full analytics — Overview, Plans and Exercises, exactly as the athlete sees them.
Plans you've sent, plans you can send, and any plans the athlete built themselves.

body2: The share icon at the top right exports everything they've shared.

sections.title: Plans
body: Every plan you've built, and who it's assigned to. Build here once and send the same plan to as many athletes as you like — each of them follows it from their own start date.
Editing a plan changes it for everyone following it.

sections.title: My training
body: Coaches train too. This tab is your own logging, on the same account, kept separate from your athletes' data.

sections.title: Exporting
body: Open an athlete and tap the share icon at the top right. Two formats.

head: Format
What's in it
rows: Six sheets: Sessions, Set log, Exercises, Check-ins, Trackers and Notes.
One flat file, one row per set — the same data as the Set log sheet.

sections.tip: Custom per-set fields you've defined become their own columns in both formats.

sections.title: Settings
body: Your display name, theme and accent colour, the custom per-set fields your athletes see when logging, and the switch to the athlete side of your account.

parts.title: 6. Good to know
parts.intro: The bits that don't belong to any one screen.

sections.title: XP, levels, streaks and quests
body: Everything you log earns XP, and XP raises your level. Nothing here changes your training — it's just there to make showing up feel like it counts.

head: What you did
XP
rows: 25 each, plus 75 for all of them

body2: Your streak counts days in a row with training. Rest days that your plan schedules bridge the streak instead of breaking it.
Quests refresh weekly — things like training three days, logging twelve exercises, or lifting five tonnes of volume.

sections.title: Who can see what
body: Your logs are yours. A coach only sees them once you've linked to them and left "Share logs with my coach" switched on for that coach.
You can also mark a single session private while logging it — it stays out of everything your coach sees, but still counts toward your own totals.
Coaches never see your email address.

sections.title: Two coaches at once
body: You can link more than one coach. Each coach's plan shows up as its own block on your Home screen, and you choose separately for each coach whether they can see your logs.

head: Goal
Where to go
rows: Log a workout from last Tuesday
Home, then the back arrow on the date bar until you reach it
Log something not in my plan
Home, bottom of the screen, Extra work
See if my bench press is improving
Progress, Exercises tab, tap Flat bench press
See everything I did in one session
Progress, Plans tab, pick the plan, pick the session
Progress, then switch the chip at the top between them
Change how an exercise is logged
Settings, Exercise library, tap the exercise
Stop my coach seeing my logs
Settings, Coaches, switch off Share logs
Coach side: open the athlete and tap the share icon
Train and coach on one account

head: Word
Means
rows: Your training week — which days, and what's on each.
One week of a plan. A 4-week plan cycles back to week 1 after week 4.
One round of an exercise — for example 60 kg for 10 reps.
Weight times reps, added up. The usual measure of how much work you did.
Your top number for an exercise that day — heaviest weight, longest distance, or longest hold.
A guess at the most you could lift once, worked out from your weight and reps.
How hard a set felt, 1 to 10.
How much of the planned work actually got done.
A session written up after the day it happened. It still counts.

sections.title: If something looks wrong
body: Charts are empty: you need at least two sessions before a trend line can be drawn.
A plan shows nothing on Home: check its start date — a plan schedules nothing before the day it begins.
Your coach can't see a session: check that it isn't marked private, and that Share logs is on for that coach in Settings.
An exercise asks for the wrong boxes: change its logging method in Settings, under Exercise library.
